title: Union Minister, Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh and Shri Suvendu Adhikari, Chief Minister, West Bengal to Co-Chair Review meeting on implementation of Schemes and Programmes for development of fisheries and aquaculture in West Bengal
subtitle: Focus on charting Roadmap for Sustainable Growth of the Fisheries Sector by Enhancing Production, Strengthening Market Linkages and Fisheries Value Chain Development
body_text:
The Department of Fisheries, Government of India is organizing a Review Meeting on Development of Fisheries in West Bengal on 21 st September 2026 in Kolkata, West Bengal co-chaired by Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh , Hon’ble Union Minister for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying and Panchayati Raj and Shri Suvendu Adhikari, Hon'ble Chief Minister, West Bengal. After more than a decade, an apex level fisheries review meeting is being organized to chalk out roadmap for huge untapped fisheries potential in West Bengal.
The review meeting will be held in the gracious presence of Shri Rajesh Mahata , Hon'ble Minister of State (Independent Charge) Department of ARD & Fisheries, Government of West Bengal. The meeting will also witnessed participation from officials from Department of Fisheries, GoI, West Bengal state fisheries department, National Fisheries Development Board (NFDB), ICAR institutes, NBFGR, CIFE, NABARD, NCDC, CAA, EIC, Indian Coast Guard and MPEDA.
The meeting will provide a comprehensive platform to review the progress of various schemes and programs in West Bengal and deliberate on key focus areas for its future development. Presentations by the Department of Fisheries, Government of India and the Government of West Bengal, along with interactions with leading fisheries research, regulatory and financial institutions, will facilitate discussions on production enhancement, aquaculture expansion, technology adoption, infrastructure development, institutional support and investment promotion followed by the handing over of the Administrative Approval for Integrated Reservoir Development in West Bengal. The deliberations are expected to help identify priority interventions and strengthen Centre-State collaboration for accelerating sustainable and inclusive growth of the fisheries sector in West Bengal.
West Bengal, the second largest fish producing state in the country, possesses vast fisheries potential, contributed to 25.43 Lakh ton of fish production in 2025-26. The increase in production is supported by an investment of Rs 617 Crore made under various schemes strengthening production technologies, Post harvest infrastructure, processing and capacity building providing livelihood opportunities to more than 30 lakh fisher folks and developing a robust fisheries ecosystem supported by value chain and market access . The government of India has also notified 34 fisheries production and processing clusters including dry fish cluster in Purba Mednipur, West Bengal. Department of Fisheries, Government of India is giving special thrust to strengthening fisheries farmer producer organizations (FFPO) and fisheries cooperatives while also focusing on digitization of the fisheries sector through various initiatives.
The review meeting is expected to provide direction for accelerating the growth of the fisheries and aquaculture sector in West Bengal through enhanced convergence between the Central and State Governments and key stakeholder institutions. The deliberations are expected to facilitate the identification of priority areas for intervention, strengthen the implementation of flagship fisheries schemes and programmes, promote technology-led and sustainable development, and enhance investments across the fisheries value-chain. The meeting is also expected to contribute towards improving fishers livelihoods, increasing fish production and productivity, strengthening market linkages, ornamental fisheries, post-harvest infrastructure, and advancing the vision of a resilient, inclusive and globally competitive fisheries sector in the State.
